story.summaryEn: After Kimi Antonelli secured the F1 Drivers' Championship at the Mexico City Grand Prix, his Mercedes team-mate George Russell posted a statement on social media on Monday saying he wanted to "speak from the heart".
detailZh: 乔治·拉塞尔：这位梅赛德斯车手在墨西哥城大奖赛上、基米·安东内利加冕世界冠军后，发布声明表示要“说出心里话”。
梅赛德斯的乔治·拉塞尔在周一的社交媒体上发文，此前他在周日的墨西哥城大奖赛赛后没有接受媒体采访，那场比赛中他的队友基米·安东内利成为世界冠军；周五圣保罗大奖赛的各节练习将于下午3点30分和晚上7点在天空体育F1直播。
马丁·布伦德尔认为，基米·安东内利赢得世界冠军可能会激发乔治·拉塞尔的“超常状态”，或者对这位梅赛德斯队友来说意味着“一切结束”。
乔治·拉塞尔在社交媒体上发布声明，表示要“说出心里话”，此前他的梅赛德斯队友基米·安东内利在周日锁定了F1车手总冠军。
梅赛德斯车队负责人托托·沃尔夫透露，拉塞尔在墨西哥站“极度沮丧”，并在祝贺安东内利成为世界冠军后直接回家了。
国际汽联对梅赛德斯处以5000欧元（4173英镑）的罚款，原因是拉塞尔在赛后缺席了强制性的媒体职责，但这位英国车手已于周一首次公开发表了自己的评论。

“现在感觉是一个相当合适的时机，来说说心里话，”他在Instagram上写道。
“这个赛季的开局完全如我所愿，但很快就被坏运气和糟糕的表现打乱了。
“这是我职业生涯中第一个真正意义上坏日子多于好日子的赛季。应对起来难吗？是的，非常难。每周都要重新振作起来难吗？是的，非常难。有时会感到困惑吗？经常。我只知道我已经倾尽全力，而2026年注定不属于我。”
拉塞尔上周表示，随着这位梅赛德斯车手将注意力转向明年挑战世界冠军，他希望自己能够更加稳定。
拉塞尔赛季初是明显的夺冠热门，但被安东内利全面压制，后者在还剩四轮的情况下以20岁之龄成为F1史上最年轻的世界冠军。
安东内利赢下九场比赛，而拉塞尔只有三胜；后者在墨西哥城大奖赛首圈因动力单元问题导致动力不足后，车手积分榜已跌至第四。
拉塞尔继续说道：“我想真诚地祝贺基米度过了一个绝对不可思议的赛季。你完全配得上这个冠军。”
基米·安东内利夺冠时刻在意大利语解说中的声音是怎样的
“感谢车队打造了本赛季最好的赛车和动力单元；看到大家在艰难的四年里齐心协力，让梅赛德斯重返巅峰，这令人备受鼓舞。”
“现在，我能承诺的是，在本赛季剩余时间以及下个赛季，我将竭尽全力，重新找回我职业生涯大部分时间所能展现的表现，并祈祷能找回一点运气。”
“感谢所有的支持。”

detailEn: George Russell: Mercedes driver posts statement to 'speak from the heart' after Kimi Antonelli becomes world champion at Mexico City Grand Prix

Mercedes' George Russell took to social media on Monday after not speaking to the media after Sunday's Mexico City GP, where his team-mate Kimi Antonelli became world champion; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Sao Paulo GP at 3.30pm and 7pm, live on Sky Sports F1
Martin Brundle believes Kimi Antonelli winning the world title could trigger an 'overdrive' for George Russell, or it's 'game over' for the Mercedes team-mate
George Russell has posted a statement on social media to "speak from the heart" after his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli secured the F1 Drivers' Championship on Sunday.
Mercedes boss Toto Wolff revealed Russell was "distraught" in Mexico and went home after congratulating Antonelli on becoming world champion.
The FIA gave Mercedes a €5,000 (£4,173) fine as Russell missed his mandatory media duties post-race, but the British driver has made his own first public comments on Monday.

"Now feels like a pretty suitable moment to speak from the heart," he wrote on Instagram.
"This season started off exactly how I had hoped but it very quickly unravelled with tough luck and poor performances.

"It's been the first proper season of my career where I've had more bad days than good. Has it been tough to deal with? Yes, very. Has it been tough to pick myself up week in, week out? Yes, very. Confusion at times? Often. All I know is that I've given it my all and 2026 was not meant to be my year."
George Russell said last week he wants to be more consistent as the Mercedes driver turns his attention to challenging for the world title next year

Russell began the season as the clear title favourite but has been comprehensively outperformed by Antonelli, who became F1's youngest ever world champion at the age of 20, with four rounds remaining.

Antonelli has won nine races compared to Russell's three and the latter has dropped to fourth in the Drivers' Championship after a power unit issue left him with sub-optimal power on the opening lap of the Mexico City Grand Prix.
Russell continued: "I want to sincerely congratulate Kimi on what has been an absolutely incredible season. You truly deserve the Championship.
How Kimi Antonelli's championship-winning moment sounded with Italian commentary
"Thank you to the team for producing the best car and power unit this season; it's been inspiring to see everyone coming together over four tough years to bring Mercedes back to the top.

"Now, all I can promise is that for the rest of this season, and into the next one, I will be giving my absolute all to rediscover the performance I have been capable of producing for the majority of my career and fingers crossed a little bit of luck returns.
"Thanks for all the support."

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

McLaren found significant improvement on the final runs to move ahead of Red Bull as Mercedes' nearest challenger and lock out the second row, with Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri as the best of the rest despite being marginally either side of half a second down on Russell.
Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.

detailEn: Qatar GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest in final practice from George Russell as Mercedes domination continues ahead of qualifying

Kimi Antonelli led George Russell in another Mercedes one-two in final practice at the Lusail International Circuit; watch Qualifying at 6pm later on Saturday and the Qatar Grand Prix at 4pm on Sunday, live on Sky Sports F1

George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally 'ruthless competitor' to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has 'incredible values, grace and dignity'. Watch the full interview during Sky Sports F1's live Qatar GP coverage on Sunday
Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.

Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
